myth.un: Being polite about it means you're scared to confront them.
myth.re: Staying calm and respectful is a choice of strength. You're firm on the issue and steady with the person.
myth.why: Calm firmness lands harder and lasts longer than heat.

scenarios.relearn: Calm respect is strength, not fear: firm issue, steady tone.

scenarios.hook: "Screenshot it and post it so everyone sees what he said."

myth.un: Screenshot it and post it so everyone sees what he said.
myth.re: Posting it to shame him entrenches him; a private message about how it landed is more likely to change him.
myth.why: Public exposure triggers defence; private feedback invites a rethink.

scenarios.relearn: Shaming a screenshot entrenches; a private note about impact changes minds.

scenarios.hook: "If he doesn't apologise instantly, the call-in failed."

myth.un: If he doesn't apologise instantly, the call-in failed.
myth.re: Minds usually shift slowly. A good call-in plants a seed; the change often shows up later, not on the spot.
myth.why: Real reflection takes time; an instant reaction isn't the only sign it worked.

scenarios.relearn: A call-in plants a seed; change often shows up later, not instantly.

scenarios.hook: "Calling in is just letting harmful people off easy."

myth.un: Calling in is just letting harmful people off easy.
myth.re: Serious harm still gets named firmly. Call-in is the default for honest slips, not a free pass for real harm.
myth.why: You can be persuasive with a slip and firm with genuine harm.

scenarios.relearn: Call-in is the default for honest slips; real harm is named firmly.

scenarios.hook: "Tell off the relative at dinner so the whole family hears it."

myth.un: Tell off the relative at dinner so the whole family hears it.
myth.re: A quiet word later, respecting the relationship, usually shifts an elder more than a scene at the table.
myth.why: Public confrontation in a family hardens elders; a respectful aside keeps the door open.

scenarios.relearn: A respectful private word shifts a relative better than a family scene.

scenarios.hook: In the class group chat, a boy posts a girls-can't-drive meme and everyone laughs.

steps.prompt: Messages keep piling in. What do you do?

options.text: DM him: "Not a fan of that one. Can we skip those?"
options.then: He replies with a thumbs up. "Okay, fair." The chat never sees it.

options.text: Reply in the chat that he's sexist, for all to see
options.then: He fires back that it's a joke, and the chat splits into sides.

options.text: React with a laughing emoji and keep scrolling
options.then: The meme gets more reactions. He posts another one soon.

options.text: Ask the group admin to delete it, nothing more
options.then: The admin deletes it. He's puzzled and posts a fresh one next week.

steps.why: A private, kind note lets him step back without an audience.

steps.prompt: A girl from the class messages you that the memes bother her. What do you do?

options.text: Thank her, and offer to back her if she raises it
options.then: She says she'd like that. She feels less alone in the chat.

options.text: Tell her to ignore it, since boys will be boys
options.then: She types something, deletes it and goes quiet for now.

options.text: Screenshot her message and post it in the chat
options.then: The chat erupts. She's upset you exposed her, and it takes days before she writes again.

options.text: Say you'll sort it out and she needn't do a thing
options.then: She thanks you, though she'd hoped to have a say.

steps.why: Believing her and backing her choice gives her support without taking over.

steps.prompt: Days later, another meme lands. The girl asks how she could raise it with him. What do you suggest?

options.text: A short, calm message, with you standing by her
options.then: She sends it. He replies, "Didn't realise. Sorry."

options.text: A long message listing every meme he has posted
options.then: He feels attacked and replies with a shrug emoji.

options.text: Post it in the chat so everyone sees
options.then: The chat piles on him, and he doubles down.

options.text: Skip it, since he won't change anyway
options.then: She nods and puts her phone down. The memes carry on.

steps.why: A calm, short message is easier to hear than a long list or a pile-on.

scenarios.debrief: A private nudge in good faith moves a peer better than a public label.
scenarios.relearn: Message a peer privately and kindly, not call them out in the group.

scenarios.hook: A senior on your project team keeps calling Ria, the only girl and your data lead, "the typist".

steps.prompt: He did it again at today's meeting. What do you do?

options.text: Catch him after: "She's our data lead." Use her title.
options.then: He hears it without an audience. "Okay, fine," he says.

options.text: Snap at him in front of everyone
options.then: He snaps back, and the team watches in silence.

options.text: Say nothing, since he's a senior
options.then: He takes the quiet as approval. The nickname sticks.

options.text: Tell Ria to just ignore him
options.then: Ria says nothing. You can tell it didn't help.

steps.why: A quiet, respectful word protects her role without humiliating him.

steps.prompt: Ria later says the nickname has been getting to her. What do you do?

options.text: Listen, and offer to back her if she raises it
options.then: Ria relaxes. "I'd like to say it myself, with you there."

options.text: Tell her he doesn't mean it
options.then: Ria goes quiet and says never mind.

options.text: Say you'll handle it so she needn't do anything
options.then: Ria nods, though she wanted a say.

options.text: Suggest she ask to switch teams
options.then: Ria stiffens. "Why should I be the one to leave?"

steps.why: Listening and offering backup respects her choices.

steps.prompt: At the next meeting, he talks over Ria's data. What do you do?

options.text: Say, "Let her finish. This is her analysis."
options.then: He pauses. "Right, go on, Ria." She carries on, steadier.

options.text: Wait it out and complain to others later
options.then: Ria's point is lost, and the complaint reaches nobody useful.

options.text: Interrupt him back, loudly
options.then: The meeting turns into a shouting match. The data is forgotten.

options.text: Let it pass, since she can handle it
options.then: Ria loses her thread and her slot runs out.

steps.why: Handing the floor back is calm and clear, and it's her work being heard.

scenarios.debrief: A quiet, respectful correction protects her role without humiliating him.
scenarios.relearn: Correct a put-down privately and respectfully, even with a senior.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Aman jokes that a classmate "throws like a girl". He means no harm.

steps.prompt: The group laughs, and Aman grins at you. What do you do?

options.text: Say quietly it's a joke, but it puts girls down
options.then: He blinks. "Huh. I never thought of it like that."

options.text: Announce to the group that Aman is a sexist
options.then: Aman argues back, loudly, and the group stops listening.

options.text: Laugh a little so he doesn't feel judged
options.then: Aman grins wider. He thinks you're on his side.

options.text: Change the subject to the match on Sunday
options.then: The talk moves on. The joke is never questioned.

steps.why: Naming the impact quietly lets him hear it without defending himself.

steps.prompt: A week later, Aman says it again at the nets. What do you do?

options.text: Say, "That one again? Let's retire it."
options.then: Aman groans, then grins. "Fine, retired."

options.text: Say nothing, so the group stays easy
options.then: The joke gets a few laughs, and it feels normal.

options.text: Throw the same joke back at him
options.then: The group laughs. Now the joke is the game.

options.text: Ask the coach to ban the phrase
options.then: The coach has a word with Aman. He rolls his eyes, since you never told him yourself why it matters.

steps.why: A light, clear nudge keeps the friendship and the point.

steps.prompt: A girl from the team overhears and looks away. What do you do?

options.text: Check in with her, and say it's not okay with you
options.then: She gives a small smile. "Thanks. It gets old."

options.text: Tell Aman to apologise to her right now
options.then: Aman does it stiffly. She's embarrassed to be the centre.

options.text: Pretend you didn't notice anything
options.then: She walks off. You wonder if she thinks you agree.

options.text: Tell her not to take it so seriously
options.then: Her smile fades. "Right," she says.

steps.why: Checking in shows where you stand without putting her on the spot.

scenarios.debrief: Assuming good faith and naming the impact invites a friend to rethink.
scenarios.relearn: Name the impact gently, assuming good faith, instead of labelling.

scenarios.hook: On your fest committee, Rohit keeps brushing off every idea the girls suggest.

steps.prompt: Today he cuts off another idea within seconds. What do you do?

options.text: Tell him privately their ideas get cut fast
options.then: Rohit blinks. "Do I? Maybe I do." He says he'll listen next time.

options.text: Call him biased in the middle of the meeting
options.then: Rohit defends himself loudly. The idea is forgotten.

options.text: Quietly agree with him so the meeting ends sooner
options.then: The meeting ends on time, and the idea dies in silence.

options.text: Message the committee head to remove him
options.then: The head is surprised. Rohit hears about it from someone else.

steps.why: Naming a pattern privately, as a shared problem, opens change.

steps.prompt: At the next meeting, Rohit is about to dismiss Tara's idea. What do you do?

options.text: Say, "Hang on, let Tara finish her idea."
options.then: Rohit shrugs and listens. Tara gets the full minute she needed.

options.text: Wait and see if he improves by himself
options.then: He doesn't. Tara stops sharing her ideas.

options.text: Repeat Tara's idea as if it were yours
options.then: It's accepted at once. Tara notices who got the credit.

options.text: Sigh loudly and roll your eyes at him
options.then: Rohit sees it and gets defensive.

steps.why: Making room for her to finish gets her idea heard under her own name.

steps.prompt: Later, you bring the pattern up with Rohit, and he says you're making it a gender thing. What do you say?

options.text: "It's a we problem. Let's track whose ideas pass."
options.then: Rohit agrees to track it. The list shows how few of theirs were used.

options.text: "Yes it is, and you're the problem."
options.then: Rohit crosses his arms. The talk ends there.

options.text: Say maybe he's right, and drop it
options.then: He's relieved. Nothing changes in the next meeting.

options.text: "Everyone else on the committee agrees with me."
options.then: Rohit frowns. "Who said that?" He trusts you less now.

steps.why: A shared task keeps it a team problem and gives him a way to see it.

scenarios.debrief: Naming a pattern privately, as something to fix together, opens change.
scenarios.relearn: Point out a pattern privately as a 'we' problem, not a public charge.

scenarios.hook: Last week you called Nikhil in over a joke, and now he's prickly about it.

steps.prompt: He says he can't even joke now. What do you say?

options.text: "You can joke, just not at someone's cost. We're good."
options.then: Nikhil's shoulders drop. "Okay. That's fair."

options.text: "Obviously not. Grow up and stop being so touchy."
options.then: Nikhil snaps back, and your call-in becomes a fight.

options.text: "Sorry I said anything at all. Forget the whole thing."
options.then: He's relieved. The joke he made stays unchallenged.

options.text: "Whatever. Joke all you like, then."
options.then: He mutters that you're being weird. The air stays tense.

steps.why: Holding the line warmly keeps both the friend and the point.

steps.prompt: At lunch, Nikhil tells a joke at a girl's expense. What do you do?

options.text: Don't laugh, and say "That one's at her cost."
options.then: Nikhil winces. "Okay, got it." He tries a different one.

options.text: Laugh hard to show you're over it
options.then: The table laughs along. He's sure the line has moved.

options.text: Say "There he goes again" to the whole table
options.then: Nikhil's face falls. The table goes quiet, and he feels mocked.

options.text: Walk out of lunch without a word
options.then: Nikhil notices. He feels judged, not guided.

steps.why: A short, calm word names the line without turning on him.

steps.prompt: Nikhil asks if you're still annoyed with him. What do you say?

options.text: Say no. You like his humour and want it kind
options.then: He smiles. "Deal. Kind and funny, then."

options.text: Say yes, and you'll be watching him
options.then: Nikhil gets quiet. He starts censoring himself around you.

options.text: Say it's fine. You've got used to it
options.then: He grins, and the jokes get sharper again.

options.text: Say you'll stay quiet if he tones it down
options.then: He agrees, but it feels like a deal rather than a change.

steps.why: Saying plainly that you value him and the kindness keeps the door open.

scenarios.debrief: Holding the line warmly keeps both the person and the point.
scenarios.relearn: Hold the boundary warmly: joke, yes; at someone's cost, no.

scenarios.hook: At a wedding, an uncle loudly says your cousin Pooja should drop her job after marriage.

steps.prompt: Guests nod, and Pooja smiles stiffly. What do you do?

options.text: Tell him later: "She loves her work. Let her choose."
options.then: The uncle grumbles, then says, "Hmm. It does matter to her, I suppose."

options.text: Argue him down in front of all the guests
options.then: The hall goes silent. Everyone is embarrassed, and the uncle digs in.

options.text: Say nothing, since it's a wedding
options.then: The talk moves on. Pooja carries the comment home.

options.text: Ask your parents to deal with the uncle
options.then: Your parents have a word. The uncle feels ambushed and sulks.

steps.why: A quiet word respects the occasion and still makes the point.

steps.prompt: Pooja's mother says she worries what relatives will say about Pooja working. What do you do?

options.text: Hear her worry, and say you'll back Pooja
options.then: Her mother sighs. "I just don't want her hurt by the talk."

options.text: Tell her mother she's old-fashioned
options.then: Her mother stiffens and ends the conversation.

options.text: Agree that Pooja should think about quitting
options.then: Her mother nods, and Pooja hears about it later.

options.text: Say it's not your place to have a view
options.then: Her mother sighs and nods. Her worry is still there.

steps.why: Listening to the worry and backing Pooja's own call respects both.

steps.prompt: Pooja asks what you think she should do. What do you say?

options.text: Say it's her call, and you'll be there either way
options.then: Pooja smiles. "That's all I needed."

options.text: Say she should obviously keep working, no matter what
options.then: Pooja bristles. "Everyone is telling me what to do."

options.text: Say you'd quit if you were her
options.then: Pooja looks away. "Maybe." Her voice is small.

options.text: Say you haven't really thought about it
options.then: Pooja nods slowly. She goes back to deciding alone.

steps.why: Offering support without deciding for her keeps the choice hers.

scenarios.debrief: A respectful private word respects the family and still makes the point.
scenarios.relearn: Make the point to a relative quietly, respecting the occasion.

scenarios.hook: A junior, Vikas, presents your friend Anita's design to the club as his own.

steps.prompt: Anita looks shocked in the back row. What do you do?

options.text: Ask Vikas privately to credit her
options.then: Vikas goes quiet. "I'll think about it," he says.

options.text: Expose him on the club notice board
options.then: Half the club takes his side, and the board gets torn down.

options.text: Let it go, since it's only a club design
options.then: Anita says nothing, but she stops sharing her work.

options.text: Tell the club head before speaking to Vikas
options.then: The head is surprised. Vikas hears it second-hand and feels cornered.

steps.why: A private ask comes first, and gives him a chance to fix it.

steps.prompt: A week on, the club page still shows only Vikas's name. What do you do?

options.text: Back Anita up as she tells the club head
options.then: The head asks Vikas to credit Anita. He does, red-faced.

options.text: Wait another week and see
options.then: Anita's name stays off the page. She speaks less each day.

options.text: Post a mocking comment under his name
options.then: The comments pile on. Vikas deletes the post and avoids Anita.

options.text: Pass off one of his designs as yours, to even it
options.then: He's furious, and now both of you are in the wrong.

steps.why: When credit stays missing, naming it clearly is fair, and Anita should lead.

steps.prompt: At the next meeting, the club head asks everyone how designs should be credited from now on. What do you suggest?

options.text: Name every designer on each entry, always
options.then: The club adds a credit line to each entry. Vikas goes first.

options.text: Stop juniors from presenting designs
options.then: Juniors feel blamed for one person's act.

options.text: Let people sort out credit among themselves
options.then: Next month the same confusion appears.

options.text: Keep a public list of who copied whom
options.then: Nobody wants to submit anything. Vikas leaves the club.

steps.why: A simple, shared rule fixes the system without blaming a person.

scenarios.debrief: Try the private ask first; if real harm stands, name it firmly.
scenarios.relearn: Ask privately first; escalate firmly only if the harm isn't fixed.

scenarios.hook: In your hostel, Kunal keeps rating girls as they walk past, and his friends laugh.

steps.prompt: Two girls pass and he starts again. What do you do?

options.text: Pull him aside: "That makes them uncomfortable."
options.then: Away from his friends, Kunal shrugs. "Okay, okay. Just joking."

options.text: Shame him loudly in front of his friends
options.then: His friends cheer him on, and he plays it up.

options.text: Laugh with the group so you fit in
options.then: Kunal gets louder. He thinks you're enjoying it.

options.text: Tell the warden at once, without a word to him
options.then: The warden talks to him. Kunal sulks and still doesn't see why it bothers the girls.

steps.why: Taking away his audience makes it easy to stop.

steps.prompt: Later that week, one of the girls glares at your group as she passes. What do you do?

options.text: Say sorry it happens, and offer to go to the warden with her
options.then: She nods, surprised. "Thanks. It helps to hear it."

options.text: Ignore her, since it isn't your problem
options.then: She walks on without a word. The group barely notices.

options.text: Tell her to report it to the warden herself
options.then: She sighs. It's always on her to act.

options.text: Laugh it off with friends afterwards
options.then: The friends joke about her glare, and the mood in the corridor sours.

steps.why: Saying you see it and offering to go with her shows where you stand.

steps.prompt: A week later, Kunal starts rating girls again and asks you for a score too. What do you do?

options.text: Say no, since you want the hostel okay for all
options.then: Kunal rolls his eyes, then drops it. One friend looks thoughtful.

options.text: Give him a long lecture on respect
options.then: His friends' eyes glaze over. They start avoiding you.

options.text: Call out a number so they move on
options.then: They cheer, and Kunal rates the next girl even louder.

options.text: Walk off and stop hanging out with them altogether
options.then: They shrug, and the ratings carry on without you.

steps.why: A short, relaxed no keeps the message without a lecture.

scenarios.debrief: Removing the audience and speaking privately ends the performance.
scenarios.relearn: Take away the audience: a private word stops the show.

scenarios.hook: You make a joke about girls at lunch, and your friend Rahul looks uneasy.

steps.prompt: The table laughs, but Rahul doesn't. What do you do?

options.text: Say "That came out wrong. My bad."
options.then: Rahul's face eases. "Thanks. I wasn't sure how to say it."

options.text: Double down so you don't look soft
options.then: Rahul looks down at his plate. The table laughs louder.

options.text: Laugh louder and change the subject
options.then: The talk moves on. Rahul stays quiet for the rest of lunch.

options.text: Ask Rahul later why he's so sensitive
options.then: Rahul shrugs and says nothing. You can tell it still sits with him.

steps.why: Owning it quickly shows others how to take a call-in.

steps.prompt: Later, Rahul says the joke bothered him. What do you do?

options.text: Thank him, and ask what bothered him
options.then: He tells you his sister hears jokes like that all the time.

options.text: Say you didn't think it was a big deal, so that's it
options.then: Rahul nods and says no more. The distance stays.

options.text: Explain that you were only copying a meme
options.then: Rahul shrugs. A meme isn't a reason, and he knows it.

options.text: Say sorry again and again until he says it's fine
options.then: He says it's fine to make it stop. He ends up comforting you.

steps.why: Asking what bothered him treats it as something to learn from.

steps.prompt: A week later, another friend makes a similar joke. What do you do?

options.text: Say "I used to joke like that. It lands badly."
options.then: He looks surprised. "You? Huh." He drops the joke.

options.text: Stay quiet, since you made one too
options.then: He assumes you're fine with it.

options.text: Tell him he's out of line
options.then: He points out you did the same last week.

options.text: Laugh so you're not the odd one out again
options.then: The joke gets a round of laughs. You feel your stomach drop.

steps.why: Using your own slip as an example makes a call-in easy to hear.

scenarios.debrief: Owning your own slip quickly is leadership, not weakness.
scenarios.relearn: When it's you, own it fast: that models the call-in for everyone.

scenarios.hook: Your classmate Sameer keeps correcting Divya's English in front of others, to look clever.

steps.prompt: He does it again during presentation prep. What do you do?

options.text: Tell him later it comes across as showing off
options.then: Sameer pauses. "I thought I was helping," he says.

options.text: Correct his English back in front of everyone
options.then: The group laughs at him, and he flushes.

options.text: Tell Divya to speak more carefully
options.then: Divya's face falls. It isn't her words that were the trouble.

options.text: Say nothing, since correcting grammar helps
options.then: Sameer keeps going, and Divya shrinks a little more.

steps.why: Telling him how it lands, in private, lets him stop without losing face.

steps.prompt: Divya tells you she's started avoiding group talks. What do you do?

options.text: Listen, and say you'll make room for her points
options.then: Divya relaxes. "Thanks. I know my stuff. I just freeze now."

options.text: Tell her to just ignore him
options.then: Divya nods, but she still dreads speaking up in the group.

options.text: Tell her to work on her English
options.then: Divya's face falls. "It isn't my English that's the problem."

options.text: Say you'll go to the teacher right away
options.then: Divya panics. "Please don't. I didn't ask for that."

steps.why: Listening and making room for her points helps without taking over.

steps.prompt: In the next group talk, Sameer starts to correct Divya mid-point. What do you do?

options.text: Say "We got her point. Go on, Divya."
options.then: Sameer closes his mouth. Divya finishes, and the group takes up her point.

options.text: Let him finish, then help her afterwards
options.then: Divya loses her thread, and the moment is gone.

options.text: Correct Sameer's English in return
options.then: The group laughs, and the point is forgotten.

options.text: Tell Sameer to be quiet
options.then: Sameer flushes and sulks through the rest of the session.

steps.why: Handing the floor back, calmly, keeps the focus on her point.

scenarios.debrief: Naming how 'help' actually lands, in private, invites him to stop.
scenarios.relearn: Tell him privately how the 'correcting' really lands.

scenarios.hook: Your class group chat is about to pile onto Arnav for a clumsy comment about girls.

steps.prompt: Screenshots and angry replies start flying. What do you do?

options.text: Say a pile-on won't help, then DM him
options.then: The chat cools down. Arnav replies, "I didn't think. Sorry."

options.text: Add your own jab to the pile
options.then: Arnav goes silent and mutes the chat that night.

options.text: Mute the chat and stay out of it
options.then: The pile-on grows without you. Arnav is shaken.

options.text: Screenshot his comment and share it on your story
options.then: Your followers pile on too. Arnav is humiliated, and a lot more people know.

steps.why: A pile-on shames, but one kind message can actually change a mind.

steps.prompt: Arnav says he feels attacked by the whole class. What do you do?

options.text: Say the comment still hurt, and explain why
options.then: Arnav is quiet, then asks what was wrong with it.

options.text: Tell him the class overreacted
options.then: Arnav relaxes. The comment stays unexamined.

options.text: Tell him to post a quick sorry and be done
options.then: He posts a flat sorry. The chat sees it as fake.

options.text: Agree that the whole class is toxic
options.then: Arnav feels backed up, and the talk turns to the class's faults.

steps.prompt: A classmate says Arnav should be removed from the chat. What do you say?

options.text: Suggest he apologise to those hurt, not be removed
options.then: The classmate thinks it over. "Okay. If he does it properly."

options.text: Vote to remove him to keep the peace
options.then: He's out by evening, and the chat goes quiet.

options.text: Stay neutral and leave it to the admin
options.then: The admin removes him without anyone discussing why.

options.text: Say anyone who wants him out is being petty
options.then: Her face tightens. She feels brushed off, and the chat splits.

steps.why: Giving him a way to make amends changes more than removing him.

scenarios.debrief: Steering the group off a pile-on toward one private DM changes minds.
scenarios.relearn: Steer the group off a pile-on; one kind DM does more.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Zoya posts a long rant calling out a classmate's sexist line.

steps.prompt: It's getting likes and shares. What do you do?

options.text: Suggest she message him directly and kindly
options.then: Zoya hesitates. "He won't listen," she says, but she thinks about it.

options.text: Like and share it so more people see the rant
options.then: The post spreads. The classmate hears about it from strangers.

options.text: Add a comment that piles on with the others
options.then: Others join in. The post turns into a pile-on.

options.text: Tell her to delete the whole post right now
options.then: Zoya feels shut down and keeps the post up.

steps.why: A direct, kind message is likelier to change him than a public rant.

steps.prompt: The classmate, Imran, messages you angrily about the post. What do you do?

options.text: Hear him out, then suggest a calm DM from Zoya
options.then: Imran cools off a little. "Fine. If she's calm about it."

options.text: Tell him he deserved it
options.then: Imran blocks you. His anger turns on the others.

options.text: Tell him to mute Zoya and let it blow over
options.then: He does, but he stews, and the tension between them grows.

options.text: Forward his angry message to the class group
options.then: The group piles on him. Imran feels ambushed.

steps.why: Hearing him out lets you steer him toward a calm talk.

steps.prompt: Later, Zoya decides to message Imran herself and asks what to write. What do you suggest?

options.text: Name the line, how it landed, and ask him to rethink
options.then: Imran reads it twice. "I didn't see it that way," he writes back.

options.text: A long list of every other thing wrong with him
options.then: Imran reads two lines and stops. He replies with a shrug.

options.text: A one-line demand that he take it back, or else
options.then: Imran bristles. "Or else what?"

options.text: Paste the rant into the message
options.then: Imran feels attacked all over again and doesn't reply.

steps.why: Naming the line and its effect gives him something to think about.

scenarios.debrief: Nudging a friend from public rant to private message is the call-in.

options.text: Tell the captain to bench him

scenarios.hook: You notice a teammate sending Isha unwanted messages, and she looks frightened.

steps.prompt: Isha stares at her phone and goes pale. What do you do?

options.text: Promise to keep it secret no matter what
options.then: Isha feels relieved for a moment. You're now carrying it alone.

options.text: Tell her it's time for a parent or teacher, and go with her

options.text: Wait one more day to see if he stops

options.text: Sit with her while she decides, and say it's her call
options.then: Isha nods. "I'll call with the counsellor next to me."

options.text: Call the helpline yourself, behind her back
options.then: The helpline listens and offers help. Isha feels her choice was taken.

scenarios.debrief: When someone is frightened, safety comes first: support her, get a trusted adult, and never confront alone. It is never her fault.
scenarios.relearn: When someone's frightened, safety first: support her and get a trusted adult.

scenarios.hook: At a school debate, a speaker says feminists just hate men, and the room goes tense.

scenarios.debrief: Reframing equality as 'lifts everyone' persuades better than scorn.
scenarios.relearn: Reframe, don't sneer: equality lifts boys too and is against no one.

steps.prompt: A week later, a classmate says: "Did you see her outfit? She was asking for it."

options.text: "Not okay. What she wore is never the reason."

options.text: "You're disgusting. Say that again and see."

options.text: "Ha, maybe. Anyway, what's for lunch?"

options.text: "Whatever. It's all just drama anyway."

steps.prompt: Mira, the girl who was harassed, overheard that and says: "I felt awful hearing that."

options.text: "I'm sorry. It's never your fault. What would help?"

options.text: "Ignore him. He's an idiot, and everyone knows it."

options.text: "Let's make that boy apologise to you in front of everyone."

scenarios.hook: A senior, Dhruv, keeps cutting off Roshni, the only girl in the club meeting.

steps.prompt: Dhruv cuts in: "Okay, so what we should do is..."

options.text: "Hang on. She was mid-point. I want to hear the rest."
options.then: Dhruv pauses. "Oh. Sure. Go on, Roshni." Roshni looks relieved.

options.text: "Not worth the fight. Roshni, just let it go."
options.then: Roshni gives a tight smile. Dhruv carries on.

options.text: "Dhruv, stop being so rude to everyone."
options.then: Dhruv bristles. "I'm not rude to everyone."

options.text: "Sorry, Dhruv, go ahead. Roshni, you can finish after."
options.then: Dhruv continues. Roshni's point is forgotten.

steps.prompt: After the meeting, Roshni says: "He does that every week."

options.text: "That sounds tiring. How can I help?"
options.then: She smiles. "Next time I might jump in first. But keep an eye out."

options.text: "Maybe skip the club meetings for a while, then."
options.then: Roshni nods. The subject closes.

options.text: "Don't take it personally. He's like that with everyone."
options.then: Roshni shrugs. The sting stays.

options.text: "You should have said something yourself."
options.then: Roshni's face falls. "I try. He talks over me."

options.text: "Not to me. But I noticed you cut her off a lot."

options.text: "No. Forget it. It's nothing."
options.then: Dhruv relaxes. Nothing changes.

options.text: "Everyone's noticed you're a bully."
options.then: Dhruv glares. "Wow. Okay."

steps.prompt: The club head asks you: "How can we make sure everyone gets heard?"

scenarios.relearn: A calm 'she was mid-point' redirects without scolding anyone.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Ayush forwards you a meme mocking trans people.
scenarios.setup: He texts again right after, waiting for a laugh.

steps.prompt: Ayush texts: "Look at this one. You'll die laughing."

options.text: "Not my kind of joke. Real people get hurt."
options.then: Ayush replies, "Oh. I didn't think about real people. It's a meme."

options.text: "Haha, that's brilliant. Send me more like it."
options.then: Ayush sends three more.

options.text: "Why are you so hateful? I'm muting you."
options.then: Ayush replies with a row of question marks. Then nothing for days.

options.text: "Lol. Anyway, are you coming on Saturday?"
options.then: Ayush says yes. The meme is forgotten, and so is the point.

steps.why: A kind, clear line says no without a fight.

steps.prompt: A few days later, Ayush sends another and says: "Someone said these are hurtful. It's only a meme, right?"

options.text: "Real people see them too. It adds up for them."
options.then: He types for a while. "Okay. I hadn't thought about who sees it."

options.text: "True. It's only a meme, and a funny one."
options.then: Ayush sends a thumbs up, and the habit stays.

options.text: "Then you're a bigot. It's as simple as that."
options.then: Ayush snaps back. "Whoa. Chill."

options.text: "Fine. Just don't send those ones to me."
options.then: He rolls his eyes. "Okay, I'll send them to others."

steps.prompt: Ayush adds: "Anyway, I don't even know any trans people."

options.text: "You might know one. Read their own stories."
options.then: Ayush shrugs. "Okay. Send me something good to read."

options.text: "Then you've no right to have an opinion."
options.then: Ayush bristles. "Everyone has opinions."

options.text: "Then it doesn't matter, I guess. Fair enough."
options.then: Ayush relaxes. The jokes carry on.

options.text: "Neither do I, so who cares about that anyway."
options.then: Ayush grins. He feels backed up.

steps.prompt: Weeks later, Ayush says: "Someone sent me a trans meme and I deleted it. Should I tell them?"

options.text: "Maybe. Say it's not your thing, kindly."
options.then: Ayush grins. "Okay. I'll send a short message."

options.text: "No. Deleting it is plenty, I think."
options.then: Ayush nods. The sender never hears why.

options.text: "Yes. Post it on your story to shame them."
options.then: Ayush frowns. "That feels mean."

options.text: "Yes, but tell them they're ignorant."
options.then: Ayush shrugs. "They'd just block me."

scenarios.relearn: A clear 'not my kind of joke, because people get hurt' is a kind, firm call-in.

scenarios.hook: At a family lunch, your uncle sends only the girls to clear the plates.

options.text: "I'll stay seated. It's how it's always been."

steps.prompt: Later, cousin Sheetal says: "Uncle always does this. It's exhausting."

options.text: "It's not fair. I'll clear with you next time."

options.text: "Oh well. It's just how he is."

options.text: "Don't worry. I'll make Uncle apologise."

options.text: "Just ignore him. He's old-fashioned."
options.then: Sheetal nods. Nothing about her day changes.

options.text: "Okay, Uncle. We'll sit this week."

scenarios.relearn: Owning fairness calmly turns a 'whipped' jab into a quiet example.
